sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, we just spent three lessons optimizing active learning to reduce manual labels. Why throw out manual clicking altogether and replace it with noisy Python rules that are only sixty-five to eighty percent accurate?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because hand-labeled datasets are unversioned technical debt! Whenever business taxonomies evolve or legal schemas change, manual clicks must be thrown away and repeated from scratch. Writing Git-versioned Labeling Functions turns data curation into auditable software executed over millions of records in hours.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Hold on! If our downstream neural network is only trained on noisy soft labels generated by heuristic Python functions, how could the neural network possibly achieve higher accuracy than the heuristic functions themselves?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because the neural network sees the full dense raw text or pixel embeddings, not just keyword triggers! For example, when an LF covers forty percent of documents mentioning superb or flawless, the Transformer learns correlated contextual features across those probabilistic labels and generalizes to the remaining sixty percent where all LFs abstained!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: In binary classification, what happens if an engineer encodes negative class as zero and positive class as one—forgetting to distinguish negative votes from abstentions?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Catastrophic bias! If abstention equals zero and negative class also equals zero, then every sentence where a specific regex fails to match gets treated as an explicit negative vote! Always use minus one, zero for abstain, and plus one—or offset integer classes with minus one reserved strictly for abstain.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Wait—if I carefully engineer five rules so they cover disjoint subsets of the corpus and never overlap or conflict with each other, wouldn't that make the label matrix cleaner?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: On the contrary! If LFs never overlap, their pairwise covariance matrix is strictly diagonal, giving the generative factor graph zero statistical signal to tell a ninety-five percent accurate rule apart from a coin flip! Overlap and disagreement are what enable unsupervised accuracy triangulation.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: How does that third term—theta corr summed over edge set E—stop correlated keyword lists from hijacking the model?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Whenever two heuristics share identical tokens or external lexicons, they agree far more often than conditional independence given Y would allow. Adding correlation edge weight theta j k corr absorbs their redundant mutual dependence so it isn't mistakenly credited as independent evidence about true label Y!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Let's experiment in Simulator 11.5A below! Watch what happens on Canvas 2 when we switch to the Overbroad Noise Trap preset: NoisyNeg covers fifty percent of documents, yet its inferred EM accuracy plunges cleanly below the precision regexes!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Right! Without seeing a single ground-truth label, Expectation-Maximization identifies NoisyNeg as unreliable because its votes constantly conflict with the consensus of orthogonal labeling functions on overlapping documents.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: This looks like magic: how can three pairwise conflict numbers tell you whether LF1 or LF2 is the inaccurate one if you have zero gold answers?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Introduce a third rule! Under conditional independence, each off-diagonal moment sigma j k equals a j times a k. Three pairs give three equations in three unknowns! Solve for C 1 2 and the exact triad formula in Active Checkpoint 1 below.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at that excess risk bound: there is an explicit label model error term epsilon g and an uncovered term one minus coverage. Why doesn't epsilon g cap our neural network's final accuracy below gold supervision?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Look closely at epsilon g of m and n! With diverse labeling functions m and huge unlabeled corpus n, the label model parameter error shrinks toward zero, while n in the statistical variance term scales to ten million instead of ten thousand—crushing variance to outperform small gold datasets!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Isn't optimizing an exponential Ising partition function Z of theta too slow when there are fifty labeling functions and ten million documents?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exact partition functions are exponential in m! That's why FlyingSquid and Snorkel MeTaL replace MCMC sampling with closed-form algebraic triplet recovery on the empirical covariance matrix Sigma hat—solving millions of instances in under one second on CPU!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look closely at Canvas 4 in Simulator 11.5B below! Notice that cyan dashed line sitting around seventy-two percent—that is the accuracy ceiling if we only ran raw Python rules directly.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Yes! Watch the solid green curve soar far above that rule ceiling toward ninety percent as N grows to five hundred, while increasing correlation rho causes orange Naive Majority Vote to sag badly!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Naive majority vote sees two plus-ones beating one minus-one and hard-labels this document positive! Surely two independent votes outweigh a single dissenting vote?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not when the dissenter is ninety-five percent accurate! Compute the conditional likelihoods for Y equals plus one versus Y equals minus one in Active Checkpoint 2 below to see Bayes' rule flip the decision cleanly!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Even with budget available, why couldn't hospital systems just send radiology reports to Amazon Mechanical Turk?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Two impenetrable barriers: HIPAA strictly bans exposing patient health data outside hospital firewalls, and radiologists bill up to three hundred fifty dollars an hour! Encoding UMLS ontologies and NegEx negation rules as Python LFs runs completely on-premise and cuts physician time by over eighty-two percent.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Wait—if five LFs derive from the same dictionary, their five votes overpower two much smarter ML models five to two every single time under majority vote!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely the correlated-rule anti-pattern! Select the rigorous solution in Active Checkpoint 3 below.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Wait—if generative models infer LF accuracies unsupervised without gold labels, why does every Snorkel deployment still create a tiny gold dev set of two hundred to five hundred examples?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because an unsupervised factor graph can flip sign symmetry if EVERY rule is worse than fifty percent, and engineers need an objective compass when iterating on new LFs! Five hundred gold dev labels take two hours to annotate—not six months—and give fast unit-test telemetry for your labeling code.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Notice how LFMetadata freezes each rule's name, category, and intended class with ConfigDict frozen equals True! Why enforce immutability on rule metadata?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because in regulated domains like clinical diagnostics or financial compliance, auditors must trace every probabilistic training label back to exact Git-committed heuristic logic and provenance tags—turning messy training datasets into reproducible software builds!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So we have seen how sparse label matrices and generative factor graphs replace months of hand labeling! What comes next in Lesson 11.6?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Next in Lesson 11.6, we open the mathematical hood of generative label modeling: matrix completion proofs, structure learning to automatically discover hidden correlation edges, and multi-task Snorkel MeTaL! See you there!
